fields.claim_quote:
Use the below inequality: For $a>0,b>0,c>0,d>0$,
$(a-b)/(c-d) \leq a/c \iff c(a-b) \leq a(c-d) \iff -bc \leq -ad \iff b/d \geq a/c$
fields.explanation: Clearing the denominator c(c − d) reverses the inequality when c < d, so the chain of equivalences is only valid under c > d, which the stated lemma omits. The selected Lean theorems certify the numeric witness (positivity, 1 − 2 ≠ 0, 3/2 ≥ 1/1, ¬((1 − 3)/(1 − 2) ≤ 1/1)) and ¬Claim, where Claim is the lemma quantified over positive reals with c ≠ d. The answer's application has a positive denominator and is not refuted; only the unqualified lemma as stated is.
fields.flaw: For a > 0, b > 0, c > 0, d > 0: (a−b)/(c−d) ≤ a/c ⟺ c(a−b) ≤ a(c−d) ⟺ −bc ≤ −ad ⟺ b/d ≥ a/c — an equivalence stated for all positive a, b, c, d without the hypothesis c > d.
